title: Quantum Basics for Cryptography
description: Qubits, superposition, entanglement, and the no-cloning theorem

questions.question: What distinguishes a qubit from a classical bit?
options: A qubit can be a coherent superposition of $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$, whereas a classical bit is always exactly $0$ or exactly $1$
A qubit can hold many classical bits at once, whereas a classical bit holds only one
A qubit is always in one definite state, but that state is chosen by hardware rather than by the user
A qubit uses four symbols instead of the two symbols available to a classical bit
questions.correctAnswer: A qubit can be a coherent superposition of $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$, whereas a classical bit is always exactly $0$ or exactly $1$

questions.question: What is a superposition?
options: A quantum state that is a linear combination of two or more basis states, such as $\alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle$
A state in which the system is classically in two states at once, each with its own definite property
A random mixture in which the system is in an unknown but already fixed classical state
The sum of the probabilities assigned to all the possible measurement outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: A quantum state that is a linear combination of two or more basis states, such as $\alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle$

questions.question: A qubit has the state $|\psi\rangle = \alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle$. What condition must its amplitudes satisfy?
options: $|\alpha| + |\beta| = 1$
$\alpha + \beta = 1$
$|\alpha| \le 1$, with no constraint on $\beta$

questions.question: By the Born rule, the probability of obtaining the outcome $|0\rangle$ when measuring $\alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle$ is
options: $|\alpha|^2$
$\alpha$
$|\alpha|$
$\beta$
questions.correctAnswer: $|\alpha|^2$

questions.question: A qubit is prepared in $|+\rangle = (|0\rangle + |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ and is measured in the computational basis. What happens?
options: The result is $|0\rangle$ with probability $1/2$ and $|1\rangle$ with probability $1/2$
The result is always $|0\rangle$, because a superposition forces the zero outcome
The result is undefined, since a superposition has no definite measurement outcome
The qubit is left in an entangled state shared with the measuring apparatus
questions.correctAnswer: The result is $|0\rangle$ with probability $1/2$ and $|1\rangle$ with probability $1/2$

questions.question: The Hadamard gate $H$ applied to $|0\rangle$ produces the state
options: $(|0\rangle + |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$
$(|0\rangle - |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$
$(|1\rangle - |0\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$
$|1\rangle$
questions.correctAnswer: $(|0\rangle + |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$

questions.question: The Pauli $X$ gate, also called the NOT gate, acts as
options: $|0\rangle \to |1\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \to |0\rangle$
$|0\rangle \to |0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \to |1\rangle$
$|0\rangle \to (|0\rangle + |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ and $|1\rangle \to (|0\rangle - |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$
$|0\rangle \to -|1\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \to -|0\rangle$
questions.correctAnswer: $|0\rangle \to |1\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \to |0\rangle$

questions.question: In a CNOT gate, the $X$ gate is applied to the target qubit when
options: the control qubit is $|1\rangle$
the control qubit is $|0\rangle$
the target qubit is $|1\rangle$
the two qubits are in a Bell state
questions.correctAnswer: the control qubit is $|1\rangle$

questions.question: For the Bell state $|\Phi^+\rangle = (|00\rangle + |11\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$, if qubit $A$ is measured in the computational basis, then measuring qubit $B$ will
options: always give the same result as the measurement of $A$
always give the opposite result to the measurement of $A$
give a completely random result independent of $A$
give $|0\rangle$ with probability $1/4$ and $|1\rangle$ with probability $3/4$
questions.correctAnswer: always give the same result as the measurement of $A$

questions.question: If both qubits of $|\Phi^+\rangle = (|00\rangle + |11\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ are measured in the $X$ basis, the two outcomes will
options: always be identical
always be opposite
be independent random results
agree with probability $1/2$ and disagree with probability $1/2$
questions.correctAnswer: always be identical

questions.question: The no-cloning theorem states that
options: it is impossible to create a perfect copy of an arbitrary unknown quantum state
a quantum state can always be copied provided enough energy and cooling are available
only entangled states can be copied, while separable states cannot
a quantum state can be copied only by a device that measures it first
questions.correctAnswer: it is impossible to create a perfect copy of an arbitrary unknown quantum state

questions.question: The no-cloning theorem does not rule out a device that copies $|0\rangle$ into a second qubit. Why is this consistent?
options: The theorem applies to arbitrary unknown superpositions, not to states that are already known basis states
The theorem concerns only the spin of particles, not the polarisation of photons
A classical bit carries no phase information that a copying device would have to preserve
Copying a basis state simply amounts to applying a CNOT gate
questions.correctAnswer: The theorem applies to arbitrary unknown superpositions, not to states that are already known basis states

questions.question: An eavesdropper tries to store a perfect copy of every qubit sent over a quantum channel and to forward the originals. By the no-cloning theorem she will
options: fail to produce a perfect copy, and her measurement will disturb the states and introduce detectable errors in the key
succeed perfectly, since measuring a photon does not change its state
succeed for single photons but fail for entangled pairs
be able to store exact copies and forward the originals completely unchanged
questions.correctAnswer: fail to produce a perfect copy, and her measurement will disturb the states and introduce detectable errors in the key

questions.question: Two qubits are entangled when
options: their joint state cannot be written as a product of a separate state for each qubit
each qubit is separately in a superposition of $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$
the two qubits are located very close to one another in space
the two qubits differ in mass, charge or some other measurable property
questions.correctAnswer: their joint state cannot be written as a product of a separate state for each qubit

questions.question: The 1935 paper of Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen matters for quantum cryptography because it
options: introduced the idea of an entangled pair of particles whose properties are correlated regardless of their separation, which later became the resource for entanglement-based QKD
demonstrated that all quantum correlations can be reproduced by local hidden variables
introduced the notion of a macroscopic superposition such as Schrödinger's cat
proved that a quantum state can be copied with fidelity above the classical limit
questions.correctAnswer: introduced the idea of an entangled pair of particles whose properties are correlated regardless of their separation, which later became the resource for entanglement-based QKD

questions.question: How many maximally entangled two-qubit Bell states are there?
options: Four: $|\Phi^+\rangle$, $|\Phi^-\rangle$, $|\Psi^+\rangle$ and $|\Psi^-\rangle$
Two: $|\Phi^+\rangle$ and $|\Phi^-\rangle$
Three, corresponding to the three Pauli operators $X$, $Y$ and $Z$
Sixteen, one for each two-qubit computational basis state
questions.correctAnswer: Four: $|\Phi^+\rangle$, $|\Phi^-\rangle$, $|\Psi^+\rangle$ and $|\Psi^-\rangle$

questions.question: The Bloch sphere represents the state of a single qubit using
options: two real parameters, the polar angle $\theta$ and the azimuthal angle $\phi$
four real parameters, one for each possible computational basis outcome
three real parameters, since a qubit needs three independent complex amplitudes
one real parameter, since only $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$ can occur in an experiment
questions.correctAnswer: two real parameters, the polar angle $\theta$ and the azimuthal angle $\phi$

questions.question: Which pair of states differs by a relative phase of $\pi$?
options: $|+\rangle = (|0\rangle + |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ and $|-\rangle = (|0\rangle - |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$
$|+\rangle$ and $i|+\rangle$
$|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$
$|00\rangle$ and $|01\rangle$
questions.correctAnswer: $|+\rangle = (|0\rangle + |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ and $|-\rangle = (|0\rangle - |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$

questions.question: Two states $|\psi\rangle$ and $e^{i\theta}|\psi\rangle$ differ only by a global phase. This means
options: they are physically equivalent, since every measurement outcome probability is identical for both
they are different states that interfere differently inside an interferometer
only one of the two can be prepared by a physical apparatus
the two states are orthogonal to one another
questions.correctAnswer: they are physically equivalent, since every measurement outcome probability is identical for both

questions.question: Quantum interference arises because
options: probability amplitudes along alternative paths add before squaring, so they can reinforce or cancel
classical probabilities along alternative paths add before squaring
the particles collide with each other and scatter into new paths
the measuring apparatus introduces random noise into the observed result
questions.correctAnswer: probability amplitudes along alternative paths add before squaring, so they can reinforce or cancel

questions.question: A system of $n$ qubits has a Hilbert space of dimension
options: 4 for any $n \ge 2$

questions.question: In the Copenhagen description, a measurement of a qubit in a superposition state
options: produces one definite outcome, and the state after the measurement is the corresponding basis state
leaves the state as the original superposition, but now with a known value
produces all possible outcomes at once, each carrying its probability amplitude
destroys the state so completely that no further measurement is possible
questions.correctAnswer: produces one definite outcome, and the state after the measurement is the corresponding basis state

questions.question: A qubit in the state $|-\rangle = (|0\rangle - |1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ is measured in the computational basis. The result is
options: $|0\rangle$ with probability $1/2$ and $|1\rangle$ with probability $1/2$
$|0\rangle$ with probability $1$
$|1\rangle$ with probability $1$
always $|-\rangle$, since the state is unchanged by the measurement
questions.correctAnswer: $|0\rangle$ with probability $1/2$ and $|1\rangle$ with probability $1/2$

questions.question: Which statement correctly contrasts quantum gates with measurement?
options: Quantum gates are unitary and reversible, while measurement is irreversible and destroys the phase information
Quantum gates are irreversible in the same way as measurement, because both create entropy
Both are reversible, so any measurement can be undone by applying a Hadamard gate
Quantum gates are deterministic only when the input state is an eigenstate of the gate
questions.correctAnswer: Quantum gates are unitary and reversible, while measurement is irreversible and destroys the phase information

questions.question: A qubit in an equal classical mixture of $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$ differs from the superposition $|+\rangle$ because the mixture
options: shows no interference and no entanglement-like correlation, whereas a coherent superposition does
cannot be described by a wave function at all
must always be prepared by a classical random source and never by a quantum gate
has a larger Hilbert space than a coherent superposition of the same two states
questions.correctAnswer: shows no interference and no entanglement-like correlation, whereas a coherent superposition does
